seoTitle: How to Choose Restaurant POS Software in Pakistan
metaDescription: Compare restaurant POS software using a practical demo checklist for orders, devices, stock, riders, reporting and the full cost of your Pakistan setup.
h1: How to Choose Restaurant POS Software in Pakistan
outline: H2 Write a one-page operating brief
H3 Identify the handoffs that cause rework
H2 Run the same demonstration with each vendor
H2 Verify devices and integrations explicitly
H3 Test interruptions as well as normal service
H2 Include stock, riders and branches
H2 Compare the complete cost
H2 Check reporting
H2 Agree a controlled rollout
evidenceRequired: Owner-approved pricing and existing product descriptions used; no performance results claimed.
Optional improvement: approved recorded demo and device compatibility evidence.
cta: Bring your own records and requirements to a free Restrova demo: /contact
draft:
Choosing restaurant POS software in Pakistan starts with a practical question: can your team complete a normal service, including the awkward orders, without losing track of what happened? A feature list helps you shortlist systems. A repeatable demonstration helps you decide whether one fits your restaurant.

This guide is for owners comparing a first POS or replacing an existing system. It is a buying method, not a certification of any vendor's hardware, tax integration or offline capability.

## 1. Write a one-page operating brief

List your order sources: counter, phone, website, branded app and any marketplace. Record how many branches you operate, who takes orders, who prepares them and who closes the shift. Separate what you need today from a possible future expansion.

Bring a sample menu with a required modifier, an unavailable item and a price that differs between branches, if that reflects your operation. Use sample customer details for testing rather than real customers' personal information.

### Identify the handoffs that cause rework

Choose one recurring problem to investigate: a counter order that reaches preparation late, an online order that is retyped, or a rider payment that is difficult to reconcile. Describe the steps and the people involved. Avoid turning the brief into a long list of features nobody will use.

## 2. Run the same demonstration with each vendor

Ask the vendor to follow your sample order from entry to the final record. Start with a counter order, then compare an online order. Look for a clear order reference, correct item options, the intended branch and an understandable preparation handoff.

- Enter an order with a required item choice and check the price.
- Find an online order and identify who is responsible for it.
- Change preparation status and review what staff can see.
- Review pickup or delivery according to your operation.
- Follow a cancellation or correction into the report.

Record whether each requirement was demonstrated, promised for later or outside scope. A presentation screenshot is useful context, but it does not show how your staff will handle an exception.

## 3. Verify devices and integrations explicitly

Share computer, printer and payment-device model numbers. If your restaurant requires a kitchen display, marketplace import, accounting export or fiscal integration, name the provider and the actions you expect it to perform. Request a demonstration and written scope.

### Test interruptions as well as normal service

Ask what happens when the connection drops, a device restarts or two staff members handle the same order. An offline claim should be demonstrated with the intended devices, including how records reconcile after reconnecting. Do not assume every cloud POS works offline or that a supported printer means every printer will work.

For tax or invoicing requirements, obtain advice appropriate to your business and verify the exact integration with the provider. This guide does not establish which obligations apply to your restaurant.

## 4. Include stock, riders and branches in the review

For [inventory management](/services/inventory-management), use your own stock units and ask how opening balances and adjustments are recorded. If recipe deductions, expiry dates or branch transfers are essential, test them individually. Basic inventory support does not establish those capabilities.

For [delivery management](/services/delivery-management), follow rider assignment, status changes and end-of-shift reconciliation. Test tracking on the intended rider phone and agree how staff respond when location or connectivity is unavailable.

For more than one branch, compare menus, availability, staff access and reporting scope. Bring the actual delivery boundaries to the [Pakistan setup discussion](/locations). A multi-branch label does not explain which configuration or commercial terms your business needs.

## 5. Compare the complete cost over a useful period

Ask each vendor for setup, recurring software, hardware, payment, app-store and specialist development costs separately. Confirm branch coverage, support, data access and cancellation terms. Use the same sales and branch assumptions for every quote.

Restrova's owner-approved model is PKR 10,000 onboarding once, followed by the higher of PKR 5,000 and 1% of monthly sales processed through Restrova. At PKR 500,000 processed sales the monthly service fee is PKR 5,000. At PKR 800,000 it is PKR 8,000. It is not a PKR 5,000 charge plus 1%.

These examples cover the stated software formula, not a complete operating budget. Confirm taxes, payment charges, branch scope and exclusions. Use the [pricing calculator](/pricing) and keep the proposal alongside your comparison notes.

## 6. Check reporting before you rely on it

Ask which period, branches and order statuses a sales report includes. Trace a completed order and an adjusted order into the totals. Review the handling of cancellations, refunds and discounts before comparing reports with cash or monthly billing.

Sales are not profit. Food costs, wages, rent, packaging and delivery may be recorded elsewhere. Confirm the [reporting and export requirements](/services/reporting-analytics) you actually need instead of assuming a dashboard replaces accounting.

## 7. Agree a controlled rollout

Name the person responsible for the menu, devices, staff training and opening stock. Agree a test service, the issues that must be resolved before launch and a fallback process if staff cannot complete a critical task. Confirm how the team will get help and who can approve changes.

Evaluate success against your starting problem: whether orders reach the right team, staff can find their records and closing questions can be resolved. Avoid treating a busier promotion or a new dashboard as proof that the software increased profit.

## Bring a concrete checklist to your free demo

Restrova connects POS and walk-in orders with direct online ordering, stock, rider operations and reporting. Review the [POS solution](/services/restaurant-pos), then [request a free demo](/contact) with your menu, branch structure, device list and the three tasks your team most needs to improve.

outline: H2 Map your operating responsibilities

draft:
Buying restaurant management software is a decision about how your team works together. A POS handles the order at the counter; a broader setup may also connect customer ordering, stock, dispatch and reports. Start by recording who owns each of those tasks in your restaurant.

Map a normal day on one page. Include opening stock, menu changes, incoming orders, preparation, delivery and closing. Beside every step, write the person responsible and the record they need. Mark the steps that are essential at launch and keep future ideas separate. This gives every supplier the same problem to demonstrate.

Ask to see the connections between modules. A customer app is more useful when staff can find its orders. A report is more useful when a manager understands the period and statuses it includes. A stock screen does not establish automatic recipe deductions, and a delivery dashboard does not establish access to a third-party courier. Test those requirements separately.

Agree ownership as carefully as features. Record who controls the domain, app-store accounts, staff access and menu data. Ask which reports or exports are available, how support requests are handled, and what happens when a staff member leaves. Confirm the account and data-access arrangements in the agreement rather than assuming them from a demonstration.

Build a complete budget with onboarding, recurring software, devices, payment charges, app-store costs and any custom work. Restrova's pricing page states the approved software formula; other charges and branch scope still need confirmation. Compare proposals using the same assumptions.

Finish with acceptance criteria: the orders staff must be able to complete, the reports the manager must reconcile and the person signing off launch. A phased rollout is easier to assess when success means completing these tasks, not simply installing an application. Use the Restrova solutions overview and free demo to review your actual workflow.

h1: Restaurant Website vs Food Delivery Marketplace
outline: H2 Give each channel a job
H2 Compare a complete month of costs

A restaurant website and a delivery marketplace can serve different purposes. A marketplace may help customers discover a restaurant, while an official website gives customers who already know the business a direct ordering route. The useful choice is the mix your team can operate and afford.

Compare complete costs over a consistent period. For a marketplace, use your own contract and settlement records, including commissions, promotions and adjustments. For direct ordering, include software, payment charges, packaging, delivery and the work of attracting customers. Do not compare a marketplace's full service with only a website's software fee.

Review who does the operating work. Who accepts the order, handles an unavailable item, dispatches the rider and answers a delivery question? An ordering website does not by itself provide a rider fleet, automatic marketplace imports or a new audience. Agree those responsibilities before moving volume to the direct channel.

For Restrova, the software fee is the higher of PKR 5,000 and 1% of monthly Restrova-processed sales, with PKR 10,000 onboarding once. Other charges and exclusions require confirmation. Use the pricing calculator for that component, then add the rest of your actual costs.

Start with an audience you already reach through your own permitted channels. Make the official ordering link easy to identify and test it on a phone. Follow a demonstration order through Admin and dispatch. Respect customer permissions and the terms of other channels when promoting your direct service.

Review completed orders, cancellations, repeat ordering and contribution after costs. Compare similar periods and account for promotions or seasonality. A rise in direct orders may reflect a shift from another channel rather than additional sales. Keep the channels that serve a useful role and improve the handoffs your team controls.

status: Unpublished draft; product walkthrough required before detailed screen instructions
seoTitle: How to Manage Restaurant Inventory and Stock
metaDescription: Build a practical restaurant stock routine with consistent units, opening counts, recorded adjustments and closing reviews before adding complex automation.
h1: How to Manage Restaurant Inventory and Stock
outline: H2 Choose items and consistent units
H3 Document conversions
H2 Count an opening balance
H2 Record changes with a reason
H3 Separate availability from recipe automation
H2 Investigate closing differences
evidenceRequired: Product owner demonstrates supported stock and adjustment fields.
Approved sample count sheet and unit conversion example; recipe automation requires separate evidence.
cta: Bring your own records and requirements to a free Restrova demo: /contact
draft:
A stock routine begins with a count people can repeat. Choose a manageable set of items, agree the unit for each and nominate the person responsible. If purchasing uses cartons and counting uses bottles, record the conversion clearly. Mixing units can create an apparent shortage even when the physical stock is correct.

Take the opening count at a defined time and record who counted it. Keep the count separate from an unexplained adjustment to the system balance. When the two differ, check the unit, timing and missing entries before correcting the record. A correction should have a reason that the manager can understand later.

During service, record the changes your process requires, such as receipts or adjustments. Agree how unavailable menu items are communicated to the people handling app, website and counter orders. Item availability and ingredient-level recipe deductions are separate capabilities; do not assume one proves the other.

At closing, count the same items using the same units and review the recorded activity. Investigate a difference with the people responsible for receiving and preparation. An unexplained variance is a question to resolve, not immediate proof of waste or misconduct.

Restrova includes inventory and stock management and item availability controls. Use a demonstration with your own sample items to confirm the available fields and workflow. Recipe deductions, expiry dates, purchase orders and inter-branch transfers need explicit verification before being included in your operating plan.

Keep the first routine simple enough to use every day. Review whether staff can maintain accurate records before expanding the stock list or requesting more automation. Connect the stock review with the manager's ordering and reporting questions, while remembering that inventory records alone are not a complete calculation of restaurant profit.

Rider management connects two moments that are often reviewed separately: dispatching an order and settling the shift. Agree who is responsible for each delivery, what staff should see while it is in progress, and how the final activity will be checked.

Start at the branch. Confirm that the order is ready, the delivery address is within the agreed service area and the rider has the details needed to complete the handoff. Identify who resolves an incomplete address or an order that is not ready. Giving an order to a rider should not remove accountability from dispatch.

Follow the assignment through status changes. Decide who can reassign a delivery, how an unsuccessful attempt is recorded and how the restaurant responds when a customer asks for an update. Live tracking depends on the device, location permissions and connectivity; test those conditions on the phones riders will actually use.

At closing, compare the completed and incomplete deliveries with the rider's payment records. Review cash collected and any agreed rider payment separately so staff can explain a difference. Keep a record of the discrepancy and its resolution rather than changing a total without context.

Restrova Fleet is described in the existing product offering as supporting rider assignment, delivery status, live tracking and payment reconciliation. Ask for one sample shift to be demonstrated from assignment through settlement. Confirm the exact fields, permissions, device setup and distribution method for your team.

Fleet software does not by itself supply riders or establish an integration with a third-party courier. If those are requirements, name the provider and actions needed and confirm them in the agreement. Review the whole process with the person who dispatches orders and the manager who closes the shift.

primaryKeyword: benefits of direct online ordering for restaurants

metaDescription: Understand where direct restaurant ordering can help, what work the restaurant must handle and how to evaluate results without assuming extra revenue.
h1: Benefits of Direct Online Ordering for Restaurants
outline: H2 Give regular customers an official route
H2 Keep menu and service expectations clear
H2 Understand the operational responsibility
H2 Measure incremental value
evidenceRequired: Approved customer journey and source records before any outcome claim.
No unverified commission percentage or guaranteed savings.

draft:
Direct ordering gives a restaurant an official place to explain its menu, accept orders and maintain the customer experience. It can be useful for people who already know the brand and want a clear route back. That is a reason to evaluate the channel, not a guarantee that it will generate new demand.

The restaurant can keep its own menu and service information consistent across approved channels. A recognizable website link or published branded app helps customers distinguish the official route. The team still needs to maintain prices, availability, operating hours and delivery expectations so that the promise at checkout matches what the branch can fulfil.

Direct orders also make the operating responsibilities more visible. Staff must know who accepts the order, handles changes, prepares it and manages dispatch. A lower software charge does not remove payment, packaging, delivery or customer-acquisition costs. Compare those costs with actual records rather than a headline percentage.

Choose a small, practical starting point. Test the menu on a phone, place a demonstration order, find it in Admin and follow its fulfilment. Make the official link available through your own approved communications and respect customer permissions when encouraging repeat ordering.

Measure whether the channel is useful. Review completed orders, cancellations, repeat orders and contribution after relevant costs over comparable periods. Some direct orders may have moved from another channel. Separate that shift from genuinely additional business before claiming growth.

Restrova provides branded ordering websites and Android/iOS customer apps alongside restaurant operations. Use the direct-ordering comparison and pricing page to assess the work and software fee, then bring your intended customer journey to a demo. This section should strengthen the existing channel guide rather than create a second page answering the same question.

primaryKeyword: restaurant POS vs manual order management

seoTitle: Restaurant POS vs Manual Order Management

h1: Restaurant POS vs Manual Order Management
outline: H2 Map the current manual process
H2 Compare the same normal order
H3 Compare corrections and missing information
H2 Include training and failure handling
H2 Define a fair trial
evidenceRequired: One consenting operator interviews the actual paper/phone workflow.
Do not invent time saved, error rates or staff performance.

draft:
Manual order management can be familiar and inexpensive to start. Its limits often appear at handoffs: someone must read the order, pass it to preparation, update changes and reconstruct what happened at closing. A POS is useful when it improves those specific tasks for the team using it.

Document the current process before comparing systems. Follow one order from the counter or phone to preparation and completion. Note where staff repeat information, where changes are recorded and how a manager finds the final amount. Ask staff about the difficult cases as well as the normal ones.

Run the same order through a POS demonstration. Check item choices, the order reference, preparation status and the final record. Then try a correction or cancellation. The comparison should include what each person can see and how a mistake is resolved, not just how quickly a salesperson enters a sample order.

Include training and interruptions. Staff need to understand the screen, their responsibilities and the fallback process if a device or connection fails. Confirm any claimed offline behaviour with the actual device setup. Software does not remove the need for a manager to review records or maintain the menu.

Evaluate a trial against a small set of observed tasks. Can staff locate an order? Does preparation receive the right options? Can closing questions be answered from the records? Use actual timings or error records only if they were collected consistently; do not assume every digital process is faster.

Restrova includes POS and walk-in orders alongside website and app ordering. Bring your current order slip or process description to the free demo and use the buying checklist to test the same tasks. Compare the full recurring and setup cost with the problem you need to solve before deciding to change.

h1: How to Digitize a Small Restaurant in Pakistan
outline: H2 Pick the first operating problem
H2 Prepare menu and staff responsibilities

H2 Test one complete service

draft:
Digitizing a small restaurant does not need to start with every available tool. Choose the problem that most often interrupts service: an unclear menu, an order that is missed or a closing record that takes too long to reconstruct. Define what a better process would let the team do.

Prepare accurate basics before configuring software. Review item names, prices, options, availability and operating hours. Decide who can change them and who checks that a customer sees the correct information. A digital menu can repeat an error quickly if nobody owns the underlying record.

Map an order from the customer to preparation and fulfilment. If you introduce an ordering website, make the official link recognizable and test it on a phone. Confirm the delivery areas, pickup instructions and supported payment methods. An app can be considered when it serves a useful repeat-ordering journey; it is not automatically the first requirement.

Use a controlled test with staff. Enter a normal order, handle an unavailable item and review a correction. Follow the record into the end-of-shift review. Agree training, support and a fallback for a critical interruption before relying on the system for a busy service.

Keep the budget specific. Restrova's approved onboarding and monthly formula are published on the pricing page. Add the costs relevant to your operation, such as devices, payment processing or delivery, and confirm any exclusions. Do not confuse a low first invoice with the full cost of running a new channel.

Review the initial problem after the team has used the process consistently. Expand only when the current setup is reliable and the next tool has a clear purpose. Bring your menu, order sources and available devices to a free demo so the discussion reflects your restaurant rather than a generic feature list.

Multi-branch software should be evaluated against the differences between locations. Two branches may share a brand while having different menus, hours, delivery boundaries or staff responsibilities. Write those differences down before asking for a central dashboard.

Use a branch worksheet with the menu owner, order channels, service area and manager for each location. Identify information that should be shared and information that should remain branch-specific. Ask which parts of that model the software supports and how changes are controlled.

Test an order for each branch. Confirm where it appears, who can accept it and what happens when an item is unavailable at the selected location. If two delivery areas overlap, discuss the intended assignment rule rather than assuming the system chooses the nearest branch or moves orders automatically.

Review staff access with actual roles. A cashier's needs differ from an owner reviewing several locations. Ask for the relevant permissions to be demonstrated, including what happens when a staff member changes branches or leaves. Do not infer a specific permission model from the phrase multi-branch.

Compare reports using the same definitions and period. Check how cancellations, discounts and deliveries affect branch totals. A central sales view does not establish inter-branch stock transfers, consolidated accounting or a profit calculation; verify each requirement separately.

Restrova's existing offering includes branch operations. Bring your branch structure to the POS and reporting walkthrough and confirm configuration, commercial coverage and the rollout plan in writing. Prepare the essentials: the restaurant name, approved logo, menu photography, prices, item choices and service information. Confirm which branch handles each order and which pickup or delivery options will be enabled. Keep the information consistent with the restaurant's official website and support contact.

Agree account responsibilities early. Record the owner of the Google Play and Apple developer accounts and the people allowed to submit updates. Review the privacy information, support contact, screenshots and descriptions required for the actual app. Store review can affect timing, so do not promise publication before the requirements are ready and the listing is approved.

Test the customer journey on Android and iOS, using the devices relevant to your audience. Browse an item, make required choices and place an agreed demonstration order. Then have staff find it in Admin, follow preparation and complete the relevant fulfilment steps. Test an unavailable item or another realistic exception as well as a normal sale.

Plan how existing customers will find the official app. Use the restaurant's own approved communication channels and make the correct store links clear. A launch announcement does not establish that customers will download or repeatedly use the app, so measure actual completed orders and support questions.

After launch, keep menu and support information current and agree how defects and operating-system changes are handled. Restrova's approved onboarding fee is PKR 10,000 once. Each month, calculate 1% of sales processed through Restrova and compare it with PKR 5,000. The monthly service fee is whichever amount is higher. The two amounts are not added together, and sales handled entirely outside Restrova are not the stated basis of this calculation.

The threshold is PKR 500,000 of processed monthly sales because 1% of that amount is PKR 5,000. At PKR 200,000, the monthly fee remains PKR 5,000. At PKR 800,000, it becomes PKR 8,000. With onboarding and one month at that second level, the stated amounts total PKR 18,000 before any unconfirmed additional charges. The minimum applies even when processed sales are zero.

Ask what the proposal includes for your branch count, devices, app-store accounts, payment processing and any custom development. Taxes and other exclusions need confirmation. Also agree the billing start date and how refunds, cancellations and adjustments affect processed sales; a calculator cannot determine those contractual details.

Compare the complete cost over a consistent period and with the same sales assumptions. Keep the operational costs of delivery, packaging and customer acquisition separate from the software component. A smaller software bill is not by itself proof of a more profitable restaurant.
